title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 1:1
body: “Here, as writing to those of equal honor, he does not set down his rank of Teacher, but another, and that a great one. And what is that?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 1
bodyEs: “Aquí, como escribe a los de igual honra, no pone su rango de Maestro, sino otro, y ese grande. ¿Y cuál es?”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 1:8
body: “He calls not God to witness as though he should be doubted, but does this from his great affection, and his exceeding persuasion and confidence; for after saying that they had fellowship with him, he adds this also, "in the tender mercies of Christ," lest they should think that his longing for them was for this cause, and not simply for their own sake. And what mean these words, "in the tender mercies of Christ"?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 2
bodyEs: “No llama a Dios por testigo como si hubiera de ser puesto en duda, sino que lo hace por su gran afecto, y por su persuasión y confianza extraordinarias; porque, después de decir que tenían comunión con él, añade también esto, «en las entrañas de Jesucristo», no fuera que pensaran que su anhelo por ellos era por esta causa, y no simplemente por ellos mismos. ¿Y qué significan estas palabras, «en las entrañas de Jesucristo»?”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 1:18
body: “None of the grievous things which are in this present life can fix their fangs upon that lofty soul, which is truly philosophic, neither enmity, nor accusations, nor slanders, nor dangers, nor plots. It flies for refuge as it were to a mighty fortress, securely defended there against all that attack it from this lower earth.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 3
bodyEs: “Ninguna de las cosas penosas que hay en esta vida presente puede clavar los colmillos en aquella alma elevada, que es verdaderamente filosófica: ni la enemistad, ni las acusaciones, ni las calumnias, ni los peligros, ni las tramas. Vuela a refugiarse como a una fortaleza poderosa, defendida allí con seguridad contra todo lo que la ataca desde esta tierra de abajo.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 2:1
body: “There is nothing better, there is nothing more affectionate, than a spiritual teacher; such an one surpasses the kindness of any natural father. Do but consider, how this blessed one entreats the Philippians concerning the things which were to their own advantage.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 5
bodyEs: “No hay nada mejor, no hay nada más afectuoso, que un maestro espiritual; tal persona supera la bondad de cualquier padre natural. Considera tan solo cómo este bienaventurado ruega a los filipenses acerca de las cosas que eran para su propia ventaja.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 2:5
body: “Our Lord Jesus Christ, when exhorting His disciples to great actions, places before them Himself, and the Father, and the Prophets, as examples; as when He says, "For thus they did unto the Prophets which were before you" (Matt.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 6
bodyEs: “Nuestro Señor Jesucristo, al exhortar a sus discípulos a grandes acciones, pone delante de ellos a sí mismo, y al Padre, y a los profetas, como ejemplos; como cuando dice: «así persiguieron á los profetas que fueron antes de vosotros» (Mat.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 2:5
body: “I have stated the views of the heretics. It is befitting that I now speak of what is our own. They say that the words, "He counted it not a prize," are of wrongfully seizing.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 7
bodyEs: “He expuesto las opiniones de los herejes. Conviene que hable ahora de lo que es nuestro. Dicen que las palabras «no tuvo por usurpación» son de arrebatar injustamente.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 3:1
body: “Dejection and care, whenever they strain the soul beyond due measure, bereave it of its native force. And therefore Paul relieves the Philippians, who were in great despondency, and they were in despondency because they did not know how matters were with Paul; they were in despondency because they thought that it was already over with him, because of the preaching, because of Epaphroditus.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 10
bodyEs: “El abatimiento y el cuidado, cuando tensan el alma más de la medida, la privan de su fuerza nativa. Y por eso Pablo alivia a los filipenses, que estaban en gran desaliento; y estaban en desaliento porque no sabían cómo estaban las cosas con Pablo; estaban en desaliento porque pensaban que ya todo había acabado con él, por la predicación, por Epafrodito.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 3:7
body: “In our contests with heretics, we must make the attack with minds in vigor, that they may be able to give exact attention. I will therefore begin nay present discourse where the last ended.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 11
bodyEs: “En nuestras contiendas con los herejes debemos hacer el ataque con la mente en vigor, para que puedan prestar atención exacta. Empezaré, pues, el presente discurso donde terminó el último.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 3:13
body: “Nothing so renders our real excellences vain and puffs them away, as to be remembering the good deeds we have done; for this produces two evils, it both renders us remiss, and raises us to haughtiness. Wherefore see how Paul, since he knew our nature to be easily inclined to remissness, though he had given great praise to the Philippians, now subdues their mind by many other things above, but chiefly by his present words.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 12
bodyEs: “Nada vuelve tan vanas nuestras excelencias reales y las disipa como el recordar las buenas obras que hemos hecho; porque esto produce dos males: nos hace remisos y nos levanta a la altivez. Por eso mira cómo Pablo, como sabía que nuestra naturaleza se inclina con facilidad a la remisión, aunque había dado gran alabanza a los filipenses, ahora somete su mente con muchas otras cosas de arriba, pero sobre todo con sus palabras presentes.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 4:4
body: “For this is the part of a teacher, not only to exhort, but also to pray, and to assist by supplication, that they may neither be overwhelmed by temptations, nor carried about by deceit. As if he had said, May He who hath delivered you in such sort as mind cannot comprehend, may He Himself guard you, and secure you, so that you suffer no ill.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 14
bodyEs: “Porque esto es parte de un maestro: no solo exhortar, sino también orar, y ayudar con la súplica, para que ni los abrumen las tentaciones, ni los lleven de un lado a otro los engaños. Como si hubiera dicho: El que los ha librado de un modo que la mente no puede comprender, que él mismo los guarde y los asegure, para que no sufran ningún mal.”

title: John Chrysostom on Philippians 4:10
body: “I have ofttimes said, that almsgiving hath been introduced not for the sake of the receivers, but of the givers, for the latter are they which make the greatest gain. And this Paul shows here also.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 15
bodyEs: “Muchas veces he dicho que la limosna se ha introducido no por causa de los que reciben, sino de los que dan, porque estos son los que hacen la mayor ganancia. Y esto lo muestra Pablo también aquí.”
